title: Introducing Strands Agents, an Open Source AI Agents SDK — Suman Debnath, AWS
talk_summary: Suman Debnath demos Strands Agents as a minimal open-source SDK where an agent is just a model plus tools, with MCP servers and default/custom tools. The demos cover file read/write/speak and Manim video generation via an MCP client, with little scaffolding and optional one-shot examples.

takeaways.technique: MCP tool discovery instead of custom glue
takeaways.what_they_do: They run an MCP server, create an MCP client, and pass the server's listed tools directly to the agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: My tool is nothing but the MCP server. And for that, I'm just using tools equal to manm client list tool sync.

takeaways.what_they_do: Agent is model plus tools; speaker suggests deleting the system prompt for the demo and letting the model reason.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The only thing that is needed is tool and the model. That's all. There is no scaffolding.

takeaways.technique: One-shot examples for complex tool use
takeaways.what_they_do: Before calling the agent, they provide an example of constructing Manim code, effectively one-shot prompting.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we are also giving some examples And if I show you this example, I'm just giving one example

takeaways.what_they_do: Any Python function can become a tool by decorating it, then the agent receives it in its tool list.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all you have to do is just import uh tools from here and decorate it with tools
